correctness.rationale: For \(\rho=\eta r/20\), the cited uniform-perfectness annular-ball lemma gives a ball \(B(z,\rho)\subset B(x,r)\) disjoint from \(B(x,3\rho)\) and with \(B(x,r)\subset B(z,2^m\rho)\). Doubling forces \(\mu(B(z,\rho))\ge C_\mu^{-m}\mu(B(x,r))\), hence the one-step reverse-doubling inequality at scale \(\sigma=3\eta/20\). Iterating yields \(\mu(B(x,s))\lesssim(s/r)^\kappa\mu(B(x,r))\), with checked exact identity \(\sigma^\kappa=1-C_\mu^{-m}\). For the cutoff \(u(y)=(r-d(x,y))_+\), small support-intersecting balls have Campanato quotient \(\lesssim M r^{-\kappa}s^{p+\kappa-\lambda}\), bounded by \(M r^{p-\lambda}\) precisely if \(\lambda<p+\kappa\). Large balls satisfy the same scale via support size; Hölder oscillation is at least \(\eta^\alpha r^{1-\alpha}\). Using assumed embedding gives \(M=\mu(B(x,r))\gtrsim r^Q\); monotonicity extends this uniformly to larger radii. Conversely the initiating preprint’s cited sufficiency theorem gives the embedding from lower regularity. All scale calculations were independently algebraically checked; the exact source lemma and sufficiency remain dependencies with disclosed inaccessible full text.

final_claim: On compact \(\eta\)-uniformly perfect doubling metric-measure spaces, the lower \(Q\)-regularity of \(\mu\) is equivalent to the continuous radius-normalized Campanato embedding \(L_C^{p,\lambda}\hookrightarrow C^{0,(\lambda-Q)/p}\) whenever \(p\ge1\), \(Q>0\), and \(Q<\lambda<\min\{Q+p,p+\kappa\}\), where \(\kappa=\log(1/(1-C_\mu^{-m}))/\log(20/(3\eta))\) and \(m=\lceil\log_2(40/\eta)\rceil\).
limitations: The exponent \(\kappa\) is sufficient, not optimal; the endpoint and the full doubling-only range remain open.
